PHASE 104 IMPLEMENTATION REPORT: DLQ API + Queue API + Nginx Routing

## Summary
Built a REST API for the Async Execution Queue and Dead Letter Queue with full CRUD operations, deployed as a Docker container with Nginx routing. Addresses GPT-4o Phase 103 findings: Critical (automated recovery endpoint), High (DLQ API endpoints).

## Components Built

### 1. Queue API (queue_api.py, 200+ lines, 16 endpoints)

#### Queue Management (8 endpoints)
- GET /health: combined queue + DLQ health
- GET /queue/stats: queue statistics (size, completed, failed, retried, rejected, avg_latency)
- POST /queue/submit: submit a task to the queue (with priority, timeout, max_retries)
- GET /queue/task/{task_id}: get a task by ID
- GET /queue/tasks: list tasks (optional status filter, limit)
- POST /queue/start: start queue workers
- POST /queue/stop: stop queue workers
- POST /queue/cancel/{task_id}: cancel a pending task
- POST /queue/cancel-all: cancel all pending tasks
- POST /queue/recover: recover pending tasks from persistence

#### Dead Letter Queue Management (6 endpoints)
- GET /dlq/stats: DLQ statistics (total, max_size)
- GET /dlq/list: list DLQ entries (most recent first, limit)
- GET /dlq/{task_id}: get a specific DLQ entry
- DELETE /dlq/{task_id}: remove an entry from DLQ
- POST /dlq/clear: clear all DLQ entries
- POST /dlq/{task_id}/requeue: re-queue a DLQ entry back into the execution queue

#### Key Features
- HTTP 429 for QueueFull (backpressure)
- HTTP 404 for not found tasks/DLQ entries
- DLQ re-queue: removes from DLQ and re-submits to queue
- Full task lifecycle visibility via REST API

### 2. Docker Deployment
- Dockerfile.queue: Python 3.12-slim, FastAPI/uvicorn
- Container: queue-api (port 4300)
- 24 total Docker containers running
- Nginx routing: https://evolvixos.com/queue/

### 3. Tests (test_queue_api.py, 17 tests)
TestQueueAPI (8 tests):
- health, queue_stats, submit_task, get_task, get_nonexistent, list_tasks, cancel_task, cancel_nonexistent

TestDLQAPI (9 tests):
- dlq_stats, dlq_list_empty, dlq_add_and_list, dlq_get_entry, dlq_get_nonexistent, dlq_remove, dlq_remove_nonexistent, dlq_clear, dlq_requeue

## Test Results
- 536 passed, 7 skipped (up from 519)
  - +17 queue API tests (new)
  - 519 existing tests
- 24 Docker containers running
- Queue API accessible at https://evolvixos.com/queue/

## Key Achievements
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 103 Critical: Recovery endpoint (POST /queue/recover) ✓
- Addressed GPT-4o Phase 103 High: DLQ API endpoints (list, get, remove, clear, requeue) ✓
- Full REST API for queue and DLQ management
- DLQ re-queue functionality (failed tasks can be retried)
- Nginx routing for external access
- 536 tests passing, zero failures

## Known Limitations
- Automated recovery not yet triggered on container startup (manual endpoint only)
- Queue not yet integrated with agent execution API (standalone)
- No DLQ alerting/notifications
- Real execution tests still skipped
- Queue API not connected to PostgreSQL for persistence

## Questions for GPT-4o
1. Should we trigger automated recovery on Queue API container startup?
2. Should we connect the Queue API to PostgreSQL for task persistence?
3. What should be the next priority: integrate queue into agent execution API, OS-level network isolation, or real execution tests?
4. Should we add WebSocket support for real-time queue monitoring?
